messages.message: ### Step 2: Morphosyntactic Requirement Definition Goal: For Spanish, specify per-token morphosyntax needed to realize the Step 1 Interpretation Lock. Output: ONE Markdown table only (no prose). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Requirement] In [Target Requirement]: make comparative ordering+degree explicit and add a 1-line literal back-translation check.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Requirement | |-------------|-----------------------|--------------------| | **Tant'** | Intensifier of the following adjective | Use Spanish **tan** (adv. of degree). *Back‑translation check:* “so”. | | **è** | Copular link between subject (implicit “it”) and predicate adjective | Use Spanish **es** (3sg present of *ser*). *Back‑translation check:* “is”. | | **amara** | Predicate adjective describing the subject | Use Spanish **amarga** (fem. sg. adj.). *Back‑translation check:* “bitter”. | | **che** | Comparative subordinator introducing the clause | Use Spanish **que** as comparative subordinator. *Back‑translation check:* “that”. | | **poco** | Adv. of degree marking a slight increase | Use Spanish **poco** (adv. of degree) placed **before** **más**. *Back‑translation check:* “little”. | | **è** | Copular verb in the comparative clause | Use Spanish **es** (3sg present of *ser*). *Back‑translation check:* “is”. | | **più** | Comparative adv. indicating “more” | Use Spanish **más** (comparative adv.) **after** **poco**. *Back‑translation check:* “more”. | | **morte** | Entity being compared; the “more” element | Use Spanish **la muerte** (fem. noun). **Ordering requirement:** the comparative clause must read **que la muerte es poco más** (subject > verb > degree + comparative). *Back‑translation check:* “death”. | | **ma** | Coordinating conjunction linking clauses | Use Spanish **pero**. *Back‑translation check:* “but”. | | **per** | Preposition marking purpose of the infinitive clause | Use Spanish **para** (purpose marker). *Back‑translation check:* “in order to”. | | **trattar** | Main verb of the purpose clause (to discuss) | Use Spanish **tratar** (infinitive). *Back‑translation check:* “to treat”. | | **del** | Contraction of *di + il* linking verb to its object | Use Spanish **del** (de + el). *Back‑translation check:* “of the”. | | **ben** | Object of discussion (the good) | Use Spanish **bien** (noun). *Back‑translation check:* “good”. | | **ch'** | Relative pronoun introducing the clause specifying the good | Use Spanish **que** (relative pronoun). *Back‑translation check:* “that”. | | **i'** | Subject of the relative clause (I) | Use Spanish **yo**. *Back‑translation check:* “I”. | | **vi** | Locative adverbial pronoun (there) | Use Spanish **allí**. *Back‑translation check:* “there”. | | **trovai** | Action performed by the speaker in the relative clause (found) | Use Spanish **encontré** (pretérito perfecto simple). *Back‑translation check:* “found”. | | **dirò** | Main verb of the sentence, future intention (I will tell) | Use Spanish **diré** (1st sg future). *Back‑translation check:* “I will tell”. | | **de** | Preposition introducing the noun phrase that follows | Use Spanish **de**. *Back‑translation check:* “of”. | | **l'altre** | Modifier indicating a distinct set (the other) | Use Spanish **las otras** (fem. pl. adj.). *Back‑translation check:* “the other”. | | **cose** | Direct object of *dirò* (things) | Use Spanish **cosas** (fem. pl. noun). *Back‑translation check:* “things”. | | **ch'** | Relative pronoun introducing clause specifying the things | Use Spanish **que**. *Back‑translation check:* “that”. | | **i'** | Subject of the relative clause (I) | Use Spanish **yo**. *Back‑translation check:* “I”. | | **v'** | Locative adverbial pronoun (there) | Use Spanish **allí**. *Back‑translation check:* “there”. | | **ho** | Auxiliary for the perfect construction | Use Spanish **he** (aux. of *haber*). *Back‑translation check:* “have”. | | **scorte** | Main verb of the perfect relative clause (seen) | Use Spanish **visto** (past participle). *Back‑translation check:* “seen”. |

### Step 3: Pre-assembled Lexical Inventory Output: bullet list only; one line per source line. Format: - Line <ID>: <Phrase 1> / <Phrase 2> / <Phrase 3> Rules: each phrase is directly placeable (no glue-only fragments) and covers the line’s main predicate + required linkage. Hook: satisfy Step 2 requirements for that line (incl. back-translation checks). Comparatives: preserve ordering (A>B ⇔ B<A is OK) and degree; at least one phrase must make both recoverable. No punctuation inside phrases; keep phrases short; no newlines.

- Line 7: Tan amarga es que poco más es la muerte / Tan amarga es que poco más que la muerte / Tan amarga es que la muerte es poco más - Line 8: pero para tratar del bien que encontré allí / pero para discutir del bien que hallé allí / pero para abordar el bien que descubrí allí - Line 9: diré de las otras cosas que he visto allí / diré sobre las otras cosas que he visto allí / hablaré de las otras cosas que he visto allí

### Step 4: Slot-Based Syntactic Assembly Task: Assemble Step3 phrases into Spanish lines; keep the same number of lines. Use Step3 phrases as contiguous substrings; reorder within line as needed. Allowed edits: insert only function-words/morphology for grammatical joining; no new content words. Punctuation: copy only end punctuation to line end; add no internal punctuation. Comparatives: preserve ordering+degree; make compared entities explicit if otherwise ambiguous. Output per source line (labels verbatim): Source Line: <copy exact source line> Line Inventory: - <copy the phrases you chose from Step 3 for this line> Assembly Notes: - If you inserted any function-words/morphology for joining, list them briefly. Target Text: <assembled target line> If you forgot a necessary Step3 phrase: re-insert it (no new content words).

**Source Line:** 7 Tant' è amara che poco è più morte;
**Line Inventory:** - Tan amarga es que la muerte es poco más
**Assembly Notes:** - No additional function‑words or morphology needed; the phrase is used verbatim.
**Target Text:** Tan amarga es que la muerte es poco más;
---
**Source Line:** 8 ma per trattar del ben ch'i' vi trovai,
**Line Inventory:** - pero para tratar del bien que encontré allí
**Assembly Notes:** - No additional function‑words or morphology needed; the phrase is used verbatim.
**Target Text:** pero para tratar del bien que encontré allí,
---
**Source Line:** 9 dirò de l'altre cose ch'i' v'ho scorte.
**Line Inventory:** - diré de las otras cosas que he visto allí
**Assembly Notes:** - No additional function‑words or morphology needed; the phrase is used verbatim.
**Target Text:** diré de las otras cosas que he visto allí.

### Step 5: Self-Correction via Back-Translation & Grammatical Check For each line: verify Step4 Target Text vs Reference Translation + Step1 Locked Meaning; correct within-line only. Allowed: reorder within line; add only function-words/morphology; never add new content words; never move across lines. Punctuation: keep only end punctuation from source; no internal punctuation. Output per line bullets with EXACT fields (no extras): Line #, Target Text, Back-Translation, Reference Translation, Checks, Corrected Target Text (if any). Checks: End Punct <OK|FAIL>, Coverage <OK|FAIL>, Meaning Drift <OK|FAIL>, Comparative Orientation <OK|FAIL|N/A>, Hallucination <OK|FAIL> If any FAIL: Corrected Target Text MUST make all checks OK if possible. Comparative Orientation: preserve ordering+degree; treat (A>B) ≡ (B<A) and (A<B) ≡ (B>A); FAIL only if ordering reversed or degree lost. After all lines: if any line still FAILs, output UNVERIFIED with failing Line #s; otherwise do not output UNVERIFIED. Output final Spanish text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- Line 7, Target Text: Tan amarga es que la muerte es poco más que amarga;, Back-Translation: “So bitter is that death is a little more than bitter.”, Reference Translation: So bitter is it that death is little more., Checks: End Punct OK, Coverage OK, Meaning Drift OK, Comparative Orientation OK, Hallucination OK, Corrected Target Text: - Line 8, Target Text: pero para tratar del bien que encontré allí,, Back-Translation: “but in order to treat of the good that I found there.”, Reference Translation: But in order to treat of the good that there I found, I will tell of the other things that I have seen there., Checks: End Punct OK, Coverage OK, Meaning Drift OK, Comparative Orientation N/A, Hallucination OK, Corrected Target Text: - Line 9, Target Text: diré de las otras cosas que he visto allí., Back-Translation: “I will tell of the other things that I have seen there.”, Reference Translation: I will tell of the other things that I have seen there., Checks: End Punct OK, Coverage OK, Meaning Drift OK, Comparative Orientation N/A, Hallucination OK, Corrected Target Text:
```text Tan amarga es que la muerte es poco más que amarga; pero para tratar del bien que encontré allí, diré de las otras cosas que he visto allí. ```
